channel.title: Kseniia's Good News
channel.description: Positive news from several sources, scored 0-10 for goodness and refreshed every six hours.

item.title: Snakebite deaths in Odisha's Angul district fall from over 100 to double digits [7/10]
item.description: A wildlife rescuer's work in Angul has helped cut yearly snakebite deaths from more than 100 to double digits. (Goodness 7/10: Real lives saved in a community.)

item.title: Bhopal opens garbage cafe where trash can be exchanged for food [6/10]
item.description: Kachra Café in Bhopal lets people trade plastic and other waste for meals. (Goodness 6/10: A small local scheme tackling waste and hunger.)

item.title: Chiricahua becomes a national park, protecting rock spires and Apache heritage [6/10]
item.description: The former national monument in southeastern Arizona is now Chiricahua National Park, protecting its rock spires and the culture of the Apache. (Goodness 6/10: Stronger protection for nature and cultural heritage.)

item.title: Jackfruit peel material removes 90% of fluoride from water, Indian team finds [6/10]
item.description: Researchers at NIT Rourkela turned jackfruit peel into a material that removed about 90% of harmful fluoride from water. (Goodness 6/10: Low-cost lab result; not yet deployed at scale.)

item.title: Mozambique safari operator wins conservation award at COP17 [6/10]
item.description: Zambeze Delta Safaris received the 2026 Markhor Award at COP17 for its conservation work in Mozambique. (Goodness 6/10: Recognition for local conservation, modest in scale.)

item.title: Portugal's last circus elephant settles into a wildlife sanctuary [7/10]
item.description: Julie, Portugal's last circus elephant, has begun a new life at a wildlife sanctuary. (Goodness 7/10: Good for one animal and a sign of ending circus use.)

item.title: Newly cleared PTSD treatment reaches 68% remission in clinical trial [7/10]
item.description: A newly FDA-cleared PTSD treatment using personalized brain mapping reached a 68% remission rate in a clinical trial. (Goodness 7/10: Strong trial result for a common condition.)

item.title: Grapevines under solar panels give larger, healthier grapes, Italian study finds [6/10]
item.description: A University of Bari study found grapevines grown beneath solar panels produced larger, healthier wine grapes. (Goodness 6/10: Shows farming and solar power can share land.)

item.title: Bird-shaped kites and googly-eyed buoys help keep seabirds out of fishing nets [7/10]
item.description: A study found bird-shaped kites and spinning, eyed buoys reduced seabird entanglement in fishing nets. (Goodness 7/10: Cheap fix for a major source of seabird deaths.)

item.title: Cambridge team builds $10 optical chip for low-cost health testing [6/10]
item.description: Cambridge researchers built a low-cost optical sensor that could bring lab-style medical tests to a wearable device. (Goodness 6/10: Early-stage but could widen access to testing.)

item.title: Kansas City's free community orchards become a national model [7/10]
item.description: The Giving Grove has planted free fruit orchards on vacant land in Kansas City, and the approach is spreading to other places. (Goodness 7/10: Proven community food model that is spreading.)

item.title: Indonesia pauses giant rice-estate project after reaching self-sufficiency [7/10]
item.description: Indonesia has halted a vast rice-cultivation project after meeting its food needs early, potentially sparing millions of acres of forest from clearing. (Goodness 7/10: Forest loss avoided, though the project's impact depends on follow-through.)

item.title: Native wildlife rebounds on Samoan island after invasive rats removed [8/10]
item.description: One year after invasive rats were removed from Nu'utele Island, native wildlife has surged in numbers. (Goodness 8/10: A clear conservation success showing recovery within a year.)

item.title: Ghanaian cocoa farmer shows forest protection can support incomes [6/10]
item.description: A cocoa farmer in Ghana demonstrates how protecting trees can sustain farmers' incomes while helping local communities. (Goodness 6/10: A local example of livelihoods and forests supporting each other.)

item.title: Bengaluru couple's swivel car seats help over 1,000 people with disabilities travel [7/10]
item.description: A Bengaluru startup makes swivel seats, portable ramps and transfer aids that have helped more than 1,000 people with disabilities travel again. (Goodness 7/10: Real, practical independence for a growing number of people.)

item.title: Six new calves born to Cambodia's Irrawaddy dolphins [6/10]
item.description: Six calves born this year give hope for Cambodia's critically endangered Irrawaddy dolphins, which still face ongoing threats. (Goodness 6/10: Encouraging births for a critically endangered species, with threats remaining.)

item.title: Ziro hosts first Bird and Butterfly Festival in Arunachal Pradesh [6/10]
item.description: The first Ziro festival drew 630 participants to bird walks, painting and forest treks that make conservation hands-on. (Goodness 6/10: Builds community engagement with local wildlife.)

item.title: AI and local knowledge help prevent tiger attacks in Nepal [6/10]
item.description: A pilot project in Bardiya uses AI to analyze deer alarm calls and map where tigers or leopards are nearby, to warn communities. (Goodness 6/10: Promising pilot that protects both people and big cats.)

item.title: New certification helps solar farms become wildlife havens [6/10]
item.description: A new certification scheme encourages solar developers to create better wildlife habitats alongside clean electricity generation. (Goodness 6/10: Combines clean energy with habitat gains, but is a voluntary scheme.)

item.title: Mozambique protects Mount Mabu, the "Butterfly Forest" [8/10]
item.description: A government decree has set aside about 23,000 acres of Mount Mabu forest as a conservation area, protecting a site home to some 200 species. (Goodness 8/10: Lasting legal protection for a biodiversity-rich forest.)

item.title: Fish scarcity drives aquaculture growth in Republic of Congo [6/10]
item.description: As wild freshwater fish become scarcer, fish farming is expanding in the Republic of Congo to supply local demand. (Goodness 6/10: Local food supply adaptation, with a modest scale.)

item.title: Rural education startup offers Rs 100 coaching to over 7,000 children in Uttar Pradesh [7/10]
item.description: Shiksha Saathi runs low-cost coaching centres across six districts in Uttar Pradesh, serving more than 7,000 rural children. (Goodness 7/10: Affordable education reaching many children locally.)

item.title: Brazil ends its customary six-day workweek [7/10]
item.description: Brazil's Senate approved a constitutional amendment that ends the long-standing tradition of a six-day working week. (Goodness 7/10: A broad improvement in rest time for workers, though details of rollout matter.)

item.title: Rare mutation may protect some people from Alzheimer's despite a high-risk gene [6/10]
item.description: Researchers identified a rare mutation that appears to protect the brain from harmful protein buildup in people carrying a high-risk gene. (Goodness 6/10: Points to possible new treatments, but early research.)

item.title: About 3,000 steps a day linked to slower Alzheimer's-related brain changes [7/10]
item.description: Daily physical activity was linked to less tau buildup and slower cognitive decline in people with early signs of Alzheimer's disease. (Goodness 7/10: Encouraging link for a simple habit, but observational.)

item.title: Touching bleached corals helped them recover fully in seven weeks in lab tests [6/10]
item.description: In laboratory experiments, severely bleached corals regained their colour and recovered within seven weeks after a simple touch treatment. (Goodness 6/10: Hopeful lab result for reefs, not yet shown on real reefs.)

item.title: Steam can replace chemical fumigants in organic strawberry farming [6/10]
item.description: UC Santa Cruz researchers found that steaming soil can sterilize it as effectively as chemical fumigants for strawberry growing. (Goodness 6/10: Practical chemical-free farming method, still limited to one crop and setting.)

item.title: 2026 Nobel Prize honours technique for controlling brain cells with light [8/10]
item.description: The Nobel-winning method, based on a discovery in tiny algae, uses light to switch brain cells on and off and underpins much neuroscience research. (Goodness 8/10: A landmark recognition of a tool widely used in brain research.)

item.title: Texas residents of differing politics join to oppose a border wall plan [6/10]
item.description: Residents with different political views are jointly opposing a planned patrol road and border construction near Big Bend in Texas. (Goodness 6/10: Cross-party community cooperation, though the outcome is undecided.)

item.title: Somerset volunteers role-play river wildlife to plan a 30-year river recovery [6/10]
item.description: Volunteers in Somerset acted out the lives of salmon, deer and earthworms to see their landscape through wildlife's eyes. The exercise is shaping a 30-year plan to restore their river. (Goodness 6/10: Community-led restoration with a long horizon, but results are still to come.)

item.title: Tasmanian programme paying divers to cull sea urchins helps kelp recover, but funding is uncertain [6/10]
item.description: A programme paying divers to harvest invasive long-spined sea urchins has helped some Tasmanian kelp forests recover, though future funding is unclear. (Goodness 6/10: Real recovery, tempered by funding uncertainty.)

item.title: Bengaluru residents, students and officials join clean-up drives [6/10]
item.description: Residents, students and civic officials across Bengaluru have joined clean-up, plogging and tree-watering efforts, including a drive that gathered 110 kg of plastic. (Goodness 6/10: Community action with local benefit.)

item.title: Fatty liver disease found to have five biological subtypes [6/10]
item.description: Mayo Clinic researchers identified five subtypes of fatty liver disease, each with different risks, which could allow more tailored care. (Goodness 6/10: Better classification may improve treatment, but clinical use is still ahead.)

item.title: Device lets apartment residents share one rooftop solar system [8/10]
item.description: Melbourne-based Allume Energy's SolShare device distributes power from a single rooftop solar system across an entire apartment building. (Goodness 8/10: Opens solar access to renters and apartment dwellers.)

item.title: Hungary repeals anti-LGBTQ Child Protection Law [8/10]
item.description: Hungary's parliament voted to repeal the 2021 Child Protection Law, which restricted portrayals of homosexuality, unlocking EU funds. (Goodness 8/10: Restores rights for many people and frees EU funding.)

item.title: California lets households choose cash to electrify instead of a new gas line [7/10]
item.description: California's Home Energy Choice Act requires utilities to offer households scheduled for gas service line replacement the option of funding to electrify instead. (Goodness 7/10: Policy that cuts gas dependence for many homes.)

item.title: Cameroon opposition party MRC elects its first female president [6/10]
item.description: Cameroon's main opposition party, the MRC, elected Tiriane Balbine Noah as its president, the first woman to lead it. (Goodness 6/10: Milestone for representation in one party.)

item.title: Three brain pathways linked to lasting depression relief [6/10]
item.description: Researchers linked three brain pathways to lasting relief in patients treated with deep brain stimulation. (Goodness 6/10: Helps refine a treatment for severe depression, in a small patient group.)

item.title: Discoverers of altermagnetism win major physics prize [6/10]
item.description: Researchers who identified altermagnetism, a third type of magnetism alongside ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism, have won a major physics prize. (Goodness 6/10: Recognition of a notable fundamental discovery.)

item.title: Researchers build wildlife pond and film Goa's first leopard cat [7/10]
item.description: Two researchers built an artificial pond in a forest patch near Bhagwan Mahavir Wildlife Sanctuary and recorded the first camera-trap footage of a leopard cat in Goa. (Goodness 7/10: Small but real boost for local wildlife knowledge.)

item.title: Stanford method restores bleached corals in seven weeks [6/10]
item.description: Stanford researchers restored bleached corals to full health in the laboratory within seven weeks, the fastest documented recovery. The method has not yet been tested on reefs. (Goodness 6/10: Fast lab result, not yet proven in the wild.)

item.title: NASA's Roman Space Telescope performs about 30% better than expected [6/10]
item.description: Engineers made a tiny mirror adjustment that aligned the Roman telescope's instruments, and its Wide Field Instrument now exceeds its performance expectations by nearly 30%. (Goodness 6/10: Strong result for a major science mission.)

item.title: Frontline workers in DR Congo begin receiving Ebola vaccine [6/10]
item.description: Frontline workers in DR Congo began receiving the Ervebo vaccine during the country's worst-ever Ebola outbreak. (Goodness 6/10: Protective step amid a serious outbreak.)

item.title: Women's group in North Sulawesi earns income restoring mangroves [7/10]
item.description: Rhizopora, a women's group led by fisher Wisye Sahambangung, helped plant 30,000 mangrove trees this year while creating income for its members. (Goodness 7/10: Local restoration that also supports livelihoods, though small in scale.)

item.title: Indravati Tiger Reserve to reopen for safaris after four decades [6/10]
item.description: Tourism in Chhattisgarh's reserve, suspended for nearly 40 years due to insurgency, is set to resume on 1 November 2026; researchers recently documented smooth-coated otters there. (Goodness 6/10: Return of access signals improved security and supports conservation tourism.)

item.title: Morocco appoints its first government led by a woman [6/10]
item.description: King Mohammed VI formally named the new government headed by Prime Minister Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, a first for the country. (Goodness 6/10: A historic milestone for women's representation.)

item.title: Brazilian Amazon deforestation falls 42% to record low [8/10]
item.description: Satellite data show 3,335 square kilometers cleared in the 12 months to July 2026, the lowest on record; Cerrado clearing also hit a low, though El Niño and the election pose risks. (Goodness 8/10: Record low clearing is real progress, with risks remaining.)

item.title: Former Akashinga recruit now a biodiversity officer in Zimbabwe [6/10]
item.description: Nyaradzo Auxilia Hoto joined the all-women Akashinga ranger initiative in 2017, rose to sergeant, earned a wildlife degree and now works as a biodiversity officer. (Goodness 6/10: A personal success story showing the programme's lasting impact.)

item.title: Colorado wildlife overpass cuts animal-vehicle collisions by 91% [8/10]
item.description: Ten months after opening over Interstate 25 near Larkspur, the large wildlife crossing has reduced collisions between vehicles and animals by 91%, data show. (Goodness 8/10: Measured, large drop in collisions protects both animals and drivers.)

item.title: Protective fabric over strawberry plants more than triples fruit yield [7/10]
item.description: Field tests found that a textile draped over strawberry plants more than tripled fruit yields without harming the plants, and with less pesticide use. (Goodness 7/10: Promising field results for lower-pesticide farming, though not yet widely adopted.)

item.title: Man turns 25 barren acres into a home for 123 abandoned children [7/10]
item.description: Shankarbaba Papalkar built a care home on barren land in Amravati, India, where 123 abandoned children now live. (Goodness 7/10: Lasting care for many children, driven by one person.)

item.title: Father and son relocate over 250 wild honeybee colonies in Cape Town [6/10]
item.description: The Cape Honeybee Conservancy has relocated more than 250 wild bee colonies in Cape Town instead of destroying them, protecting local pollinators. (Goodness 6/10: Local conservation benefiting pollinators.)

item.title: Chinese medical ship offers free care in Abidjan [6/10]
item.description: A hospital ship with 376 crew has docked in Côte d'Ivoire and is providing free consultations and medicines to residents. (Goodness 6/10: Short-term health access for many residents.)

item.title: Teenager builds disaster messaging app that relays over Bluetooth [6/10]
item.description: A high school student created a messaging app that passes messages from phone to phone over Bluetooth when cellular networks fail, aimed at disasters. (Goodness 6/10: Useful emergency tool, but still an early project by one student.)

item.title: Four Assam villages convert grazing land into a forest reserve [7/10]
item.description: Four villages in Dhemaji district, Assam, are turning 1,044 bighas of shared grazing land into a forest reserve to protect wildlife. (Goodness 7/10: Community-led conservation, still in progress.)

item.title: Free-roaming bison herd at American Prairie reaches 1,000 [7/10]
item.description: The herd on the private American Prairie reserve has passed 1,000 animals for the first time since the nonprofit began more than 20 years ago. (Goodness 7/10: A long-term restoration milestone for a native species.)

item.title: Newly described enzyme helps bacteria break down plastics [6/10]
item.description: Researchers found a Pac-Man-shaped enzyme that helps bacteria degrade some plastics; several biodegradable plastics broke down in soil within about a year. (Goodness 6/10: Promising science, but still early and not yet a large-scale solution.)

item.title: New project targets illegal killing and poisoning of vultures in Chad [6/10]
item.description: Sahara Conservation is launching a project in Chad to protect declining vulture populations from illegal killing and poisoning. (Goodness 6/10: Conservation action for threatened birds, with results yet to come.)

item.title: Seagrass meadows may give East African coastal communities more nutritious fish [6/10]
item.description: A study of 40 East African sites found reefs hold more fish overall, but seagrass-linked catches may be more nutritious for local communities. (Goodness 6/10: Useful finding supporting habitat protection and food security.)
